newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch SNS Bank plans to buy Banque Suez Nederland.
newsitem.headline: Dutch SNS Bank plans to buy Banque Suez Nederland.

text.p: SNS Groep NV confirmed on Wednesday it was in talks about a takeover of Banque Suez Nederland NV from France's Banque Indosuez.
"Banque Indosuez is considering the possible disposal of its present activities in the Netherlands," the unlisted Dutch savings bank group said in a statement.
Banque Suez Nederland is active in the securities and currency markets, private banking and corporate lending.

Its clients are institutional investors, wealthy private investors and large and medium-sized companies in the Netherlands. The possible takeover would strengthen SNS's position in institutional and corporate markets, SNS said.

Suez Nederland had a balance sheet total of 2.7 billion guilders ($1.5 billion) by the end of 1995 and posted total revenues of 71 million guilders that year. It has outlets in Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Arnhem and Eindhoven.
SNS said Suez Nederland's clients base and expertise would be an interesting addition to its own activities, which would also accelerate SNS's developments in these areas.

Suez Nederland will continue to benefit from a "preferential partnership" with Banque Indosuez and its international network in recognition of mutual interests, SNS said. Banque Indosuez is majority-owned by Caisse Nationale du Credit Agricole.

SNS is mainly active in the markets for private investors and savings bank clients but has expanded its securities operations in recent years. The bank had a balance sheet total of 27.5 billion guilders by the end of last year.

SNS said its planned merger with Dutch unlisted Dutch insurer Reaal Groep, which was announced last month, was mainly aimed at strengthening its position in the market for private clients. Thus, a possible takeover of Suez Nederland would be complementary to the plans to join forces with Reaal, it added.
SNS currently employs 2,787 people and Banque Suez Nederland has 204 employees. The takeover is not expected to result in job-losses, it said.
The takeover study is expected to be finalised at the beginning of 1997.
